title: Giant geometric nonlinear transport in inhomogeneously strained Bi$_2$Se$_3$ single crystalline slabs
authors: Igor Veremchuk, Pavlo Makushko, Anita Guarino, Muhammad Waqee Ur Rehman, Rosalba Tatiana Fittipaldi, Tobias Kosub, Alexej Pashkin, Fabian Ganss, Oleg A. Petrenko, Proloy T. Das, Rui Xu, Rhonald Burgos Atencia, Debottam Mandal, Antonio Vecchione, Carmine Ortix, Denys Makarov
abstract: Electrical transport in non-centrosymmetric materials exhibits a nonlinear conductivity tensor component that generates second-harmonic voltages in response to applied electric fields. Harnessing this effect is essential for developing zero-threshold electromagnetic energy harvesters and broadband frequency upconverters, both of which require maximizing the nonlinear responsivity. Here, we demonstrate that inhomogeneously strained macroscopic slabs of the topological insulator Bi$_2$Se$_3$ achieve a record-high nonlinear responsivity of $10^4\,μ$m/V: a six orders of magnitude boost compared to its thin-film counterparts. We attribute this giant enhancement to a classical geometric nonlinear transport effect, which is driven by complex strain gradients within the bulk material. Notably, a similar geometric mechanism known as geometric nonlinear Hall was previously observed only in microscale-patterned structures. Our findings establish macroscopic strain engineering as a powerful route to enhance nonlinear transport, with immediate relevance to a broad class of layered systems, including transition metal dichalcogenides and moiré heterostructures.
summary: Researchers demonstrated a giant geometric nonlinear transport effect in bulk, strained $	ext{Bi}_2	ext{Se}_3$ slabs, achieving a record-high nonlinear responsivity. This enhancement is attributed to classical nonlinear transport driven by macroscopic strain gradients, opening a new pathway for engineering nonlinear electronic materials relevant to energy harvesting.
main_problem: The goal is to maximize nonlinear responsivity for developing energy harvesters and frequency upconverters by studying nonlinear electrical transport in topological insulators.
main_result: The study achieved a record-high nonlinear responsivity ($>10^4 \mu	ext{m}/	ext{V}$) in macroscopic, inhomogeneously strained $	ext{Bi}_2	ext{Se}_3$ slabs.
method: The enhancement is attributed to a classical geometric nonlinear transport effect ($	ext{gNLTE}$) driven by complex strain gradients within the bulk material, rather than purely quantum geometric effects.
model_or_system: The physical system is single crystalline, bulk topological insulator $	ext{Bi}_2	ext{Se}_3$ slabs, which are mechanically strained through cleavage, creating macroscopic strain gradients.
key_observables: Nonlinear responsivity ($	ext{E}_{ij}/	ext{E}_{2jj}$), linear conductivity ($\sigma$), and rectified DC voltage ($	ext{U}_{	ext{RDC}}$).
important_parameters: Record-high responsivity of $10^4 \mu	ext{m}/	ext{V}$; strain gradients ranging from $-0.9\%$ to $+0.9\%$.
main_assumptions: The effect is argued to be purely classical and strain-driven, and that Joule heating effects can be excluded from the nonlinear signal.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the crystal structure, strain mapping via Raman spectroscopy, and electrical transport measurements showing second harmonic responses and rectified DC voltage.
paper_structure: The paper details sample preparation and structural characterization (XRD, Raman) to confirm strain gradients, followed by electrical transport measurements (harmonic and DC voltage) to quantify the giant nonlinear responsivity and derive scaling laws.
why_interesting: While the focus is condensed matter transport, the study of macroscopic strain engineering to enhance nonlinear responses provides a powerful, non-quantum mechanism for controlling material properties, which has analogues in designing quantum devices.
